en: Dhammasaṅgaṇī 2:
Exposition 2.1 Section on the Arising of Consciousness (Cittuppādakaṇḍa)
2.1.9. Indeterminate as Unwholesome Resultant (Akusalavipāka-abyākata) 2.1.9.1.
The Five Unwholesome Resultant Consciousnesses (Akusalavipāka-pañcaviññāṇa) Which phenomena are indeterminate?
At whatever time, as a result of having performed and accumulated unwholesome karma, there arises eye-consciousness accompanied by equanimity with visible form as its object; ...
ear-consciousness arises accompanied by equanimity with sound as its object; ...
nose-consciousness arises accompanied by equanimity with odor as its object; ... [and so on].
Tongue-consciousness arises accompanied by equanimity, having taste as its object ... pe ...
Body-consciousness arises accompanied by pain, having tangible objects as its object.
At that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception, there is volition, there is mind, there is pain, and there is one-pointedness of mind.
There is the mind faculty, there is the pain faculty, there is the life faculty;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate.
What on that occasion is contact (phassa)?
That which on that occasion is contact, the act of contacting, the state of having contacted,
the quality of having contacted— this on that occasion is contact.
What is the feeling at that time?

Whatever bodily unease, bodily pain, a painful feeling born of body-contact, an unpleasant and painful experience born of body-contact, an unpleasant and painful feeling born of body-contact—this is the feeling at that time. …pe…
What is suffering at that time?
Whatever bodily discomfort, bodily pain, unpleasant feeling born of body-contact, or unpleasant painful sensation born of body-contact there is at that time—this is suffering at that time. …pe…
What on that occasion is the faculty of pain?

That which on that occasion is bodily discomfort, bodily pain, an unpleasant and painful sensation born of body-contact, an unpleasant and painful feeling born of body-contact—this on that occasion is the faculty of pain. …pe…
Or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate.
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments, there are three faculties, there is one contact …pe… there is one body-consciousness element,
there is one mental-object base, there is one mental-object element;
or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial phenomena exist at that time.
These states are indeterminate … [as before] … What,
at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, one-pointedness of mind, and the life-faculty.

Or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness—this, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (*saṅkhārakkhandha*). ...
These phenomena are indeterminate (*abyākata*).
The five unwholesome-resultant types of consciousness.
2.1.9.2. Unwholesome-resultant mind-element.
Which phenomena are indeterminate?
At whatever time, as a result of having performed and accumulated unwholesome karma, the resultant mind-element arises accompanied by equanimity, having either a visible form as its object, or ...

pe ... a tangible object as its object, or whatever else it may be directed toward—at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception, there is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is equanimity, and there is one-pointedness of mind.
There is the mind faculty, there is the equanimity faculty, there is the life faculty;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate …pe….
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements,
three nutriments, three faculties, one contact …pe… one mind-element,
one mental-object base, and one mental-object element.
Or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate … [as before] … What,
at that time, is the aggregate of volitional formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, one-pointedness of mind,
and the life-faculty; or whatever other dependent, immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception,
and the aggregate of consciousness— this, at that time, constitutes the aggregate of mental formations …pe….
These states are indeterminate.
The mind-element that is the result of unwholesome kamma.
2.1.9.3. The mind-consciousness-element that is the result of unwholesome kamma.
Which phenomena are indeterminate (*avyākata*)? At whatever time,

as a result of having performed and accumulated unwholesome karma, the mind-consciousness element (*manoviññāṇadhātu*) arises accompanied by equanimity, having either a visible form as its object …pe… or a mental phenomenon as its object,
or whatever it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact (*phassa*), there is feeling (*vedanā*), there is perception (*saññā*).
There is contact, there is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is equanimity,
there is one-pointedness of mind, there is the faculty of mind, there is the faculty of equanimity,
there is the life-faculty; or whatever other dependent, immaterial phenomena exist at that time.
These states are indeterminate …pe….
At that time there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements,
three nutriments, three faculties, one contact …pe… one mind-consciousness element.
There is one base of mental phenomena (*dhammāyatana*), there is one element of mental phenomena (*dhammadhātu*);
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate (*abyākata*) …pe….
What, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
It consists of contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, one-pointedness of mind, and the life-faculty;
or whatever other dependent, immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness.
At that time, this is the aggregate of mental formations (*saṅkhārakkhandha*) … [as before] … these states are indeterminate (*abyākata*).
The element of mind-consciousness (*manoviññāṇadhātu*) that is the result of unwholesome kamma.
The results of maturation are indeterminate.
